Alex: Heads-up — observed a ~12% p95 token-latency regression on mistral14b-int8 (AWQ) after the kernel-selector change landed. Repro + quick profile below, pretty small thread but wanted to capture notes.

Alex: repro (local env):
```
REPRO=1 ./run_infer.sh --model mistral14b-awq-int8 --seq_len 1536 --batch 1 --kernelselector=auto --kv_cache=true
# load config: kernel.prefer_fp8=false, batching.microbatch_threshold=32
```

Alex: quick numbers (single A100):
- baseline (gptq-ish kernels, old selector): p50=18ms p95=72ms tokens/s=340
- after selector change (prefers new fp8-path fallback on long seq): p50=19ms p95=80ms tokens/s=300
- KV-cache eviction count spiked: 480 -> 2.1k evicts/min under synthetic chat load
- observed >20% increase in memcpy heat on head/kv dims during decode

Sara: what model variant exactly? AWQ per-layer or global quant? calibration prompts used?

Alex: AWQ-per-layer (4-bit mixed), calibration set = 200 random convo prompts (mostly short), but this run used long conversation prefix (avg 1.2k tokens) which we didn't include in calib set.

Javier: maybe RoPE scale mismatch with the fp8 kernels. When sequence > model-window we do more KV shuffling and the selector picks an fp8 fallback kernel that assumes head_kv packing aligned to 64; Mistral head_kv is 48 -> unaligned copies -> extra mem ops. 
Javier: also batching heuristic: microbatch_threshold 32 allowed bigger microbatches which increase per-step KV footprint and trigger eviction.

Emma: I ran a quick bisect on kernel choices — pinned selector to prefer gptq-like kernels for sequences >1024 and the p95 drops back to 73ms. Accuracy delta: AWQ vs GPTQ on our calibration eval: AWQ perplexity +1.8% on long-form eval set, generation-quality diff small but measurable on code prompts.

Alex: interesting — so there are two contributors: (1) kernel selection chooses fp8-ish fallback that is misaligned for this head_kv size -> memcpy/copy penalty, (2) batching heuristic leading to KV evict churn.

Javier: proposal:
- short-term: add ad-hoc rule in kernel-selector: if head_kv % 64 != 0 and seq_len > 1024 -> prefer aligned gptq kernel.
- adjust batching: reduce microbatch_threshold to 16 for mistral/mixtral families with head_kv not multiple of 64.

Sara: do we have perf counters/traces to show memcpy hotspots? would help justify kernel rule.

Alex: yes, attached trace snippet (flattened):
```
TRACE: decode_step 1024 tokens
- kernel_dispatch: fp8_fallback_conv -> 12ms
- kv_pack_copy unaligned -> 9.4ms (memcpy heavy)
- kernel_dispatch: matmul_fp32_merge -> 3.1ms
Total step: 24.5ms (vs baseline 18ms)
```

Emma: ran staging canary with the kernel-selector patch and batching tweak (microbatch_threshold=16) — results: p95 reduced to 74ms, evict rate down to 650/min. Accuracy on eval set unchanged within noise (AWQ perplexity +1.7%).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy: 2541234572 by Alex — patch eng-runtime#512 (kernel-selector: add head_kv alignment rule; batching: family overrides).

infra-bot: Staging metrics (10m window after canary): p50=19ms p95=74ms kv-evicts/min=642 tokens/s ~320 — improvement vs bad run.

Alex: ok action items:
- Javier to open a follow-up to generalize kernel alignment checks and add unit tests for head_kv edge sizes (assigned eng-runtime#513).
- Emma to run longer A/B run with traffic profile (24h) to watch regression signals and cal-sets for long-prefix prompts.
- Sara to update AWQ calibration guide: include at least 50 long-prefix convs if target use-case has >1k seqs.

Javier: I'll add perf counters for unaligned KV-copy and add a guard in the selector to prefer kernels with no extra memcpy for these sizes (should be low-risk).

Sara: thanks — also adding a quick note to the docs about head_kv packing expectations + recommended quant calibration sets. :memo: 

Alex: cool — marking this thread resolved once #512 and #513 land and 24h canary passes. Thanks! :thumbsup:
